rationale: All acceptance criteria are fully met and the core fix is correct. One blocking issue: FilterService.register uses the generic key 'custom' which pollutes PrimeReact's global filter registry — any future consumer passing filterMatchMode='custom' would silently bypass filtering. Renaming to a collision-resistant key fixes this with a one-line change. One deferred test-isolation issue (spy not cleared between tests) is noted but not blocking.

business_review.criterion: onFilter callback contract unchanged — fires on every keystroke
serverSideFilter prop is opt-in with false default — existing call sites unaffected
Server-returned users survive PrimeReact client-side filter pass when serverSideFilter=true
Searching by display name must still work — no regression (non-admin path)

standards_review.notes: Commit message follows EPMCDME-14070: Capital sentence format
No blocking quality violations; TypeScript cast is documented with a comment
No security concerns — filter bypass is intentional and opt-in only

findings.problem: FilterService.register('custom', () => true) uses the generic key 'custom', polluting PrimeReact's global filter registry for the entire application.
findings.impact: Any future MultiSelect consumer that passes filterMatchMode='custom' — whether by accident or copy-paste — will silently bypass all client-side filtering with no error or warning.
findings.recommendation: Rename the registered key to something collision-resistant, e.g. 'serverside-passthrough', and update the filterMatchMode cast accordingly. One-line change in MultiSelect.tsx.

findings.problem: multiSelectSpy is not cleared in beforeEach — it accumulates calls across tests, making toHaveBeenCalledWith assertions potentially match stale calls from earlier renders.
findings.impact: The serverSideFilter tests could produce false positives if test execution order changes.
findings.recommendation: Add multiSelectSpy.mockClear() inside the beforeEach block alongside the existing mockOnChange.mockClear().
